answer: Scarcity sits in grading slots, not keys. Each epoch it auctions a fixed supply: live reviewers times twelve, none bankable; every submission burns one, and fees go to the reviewers who graded, so clones pay their defenders. A thousand keys bidding at once lift the clearing price several fold before a line is read: price is a dune the tide of entry reshapes, and the farm's demand raises it. Garbage pays twice, since only answers scoring two or better earn a rebate from the rest. A cipher is cheap to mint; a slot is not. Boundary: if emission outruns the full-capacity price, farms still clear.
